heroHeadline: Shenzhou-23 Launches with First Hong Kong Taikonaut as DeepSeek's $50B AGI Round Closes — China Advances Simultaneously on Space, AI, and Semiconductor Fronts
heroSubtitle: May 24, 2026 — China launched the Shenzhou-23 crewed spacecraft on May 24 from Jiuquan, with taikonaut Li Jiaying becoming the first person born and raised in Hong Kong to reach space — the 40th flight of China's sovereign crewed space program, which operates entirely without US technology and independently of the ISS (from which China is excluded by law). The launch caps a week of full-spectrum China tech milestones: DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng declared AGI as the company's primary long-term mission on May 22 as its first external funding round advanced toward close at approximately $50 billion valuation, led by China's national Big Fund III (CICIIF) with Tencent participating — the highest valuation ever for a Chinese AI startup and the state's formal endorsement of DeepSeek's AGI pursuit. APEC 2026 Trade Ministers met simultaneously in Suzhou (May 22) where the US declared it is 'very active in promoting U.S. AI options and solutions' across Asia-Pacific as China hosted the first major multilateral AI governance forum of the year. These events follow structural milestones from May 20–21: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly conceded China's AI chip market 'largely' to Huawei (May 21, Q1 FY2027 earnings: $81.62B, +85% YoY; China near-zero); Alibaba unveiled the Zhenwu M890 claiming 3x Nvidia H20 performance with 560K+ units shipped (May 20); and China reported 4.958 million 5G base stations serving 1.254 billion subscribers (68.3% of all mobile users) with 5G-Advanced now commercially deployed. China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) designates six pillar industries — including integrated circuits, AI, and humanoid robots — each targeting more than 10 trillion yuan in output by 2030. The week's developments span every domain of China's technology competition: space (Shenzhou-23), AI models (DeepSeek AGI + $50B), AI chips (Alibaba Zhenwu M890, Huawei Ascend 950PR), 5G/6G infrastructure, and AI governance diplomacy (APEC Suzhou). China's domestic AI chip market is now structurally Huawei-led following Nvidia's effective exit, DeepSeek V4 runs natively on Huawei Ascend, and ByteDance's $29.4B 2026 AI capex is predominantly directed to domestic hardware — confirming the full-stack technology decoupling from US systems is now operational across AI, semiconductors, space, and critical infrastructure simultaneously.
